risk: Fictitious or duplicate customers are created, or bank and address details are altered, enabling diverted refunds and concealed related-party sales.
audit_objective: Confirm customer master records are created and amended only on authorised, verified information.
what_to_review: Authorisation and verification of customer creation and amendment
Duplicate customer detection
Changes to remittance and refund bank details
Related-party and employee matching
Dormant customer reactivation
procedures: Extract the customer master change log and test creations and amendments for authorisation independent of sales.
Run duplicate analytics on name, tax identifier, address and bank account.
Match customer records against employee data for shared addresses, phones and bank accounts.
Test refunds paid to bank details changed shortly before the refund.
Identify dormant customers reactivated in the period and test the first transaction on each.
red_flags: Customers created by the salesperson who then sells to them
Refund bank details differing from the collection account
Duplicates that split a single exposure below credit limits
Reactivated dormant accounts with immediate credit balances

risk: Credit is granted without adequate assessment, or limits are set and raised to accommodate a sale rather than to reflect the customer's ability to pay.
audit_objective: Assess whether credit decisions are evidence-based, independent of sales, and enforced.
what_to_review: Credit assessment methodology and information sources
Limit approval authority and independence from sales
Frequency of limit review, especially for the largest exposures
System enforcement of limits at order entry
Credit insurance, guarantees and security held
procedures: Test a sample of new limits to the supporting assessment and the approval authority.
Analyse limit increases and test how many occurred within days of a blocked order.
Compare exposures to limits at several dates and quantify over-limit balances.
Test whether security, guarantees or credit insurance recorded are valid and enforceable.
Test limits not reviewed within the policy cycle for the largest customers.
red_flags: Limits raised immediately after an order block
Assessments based only on customer-supplied figures
Security recorded but never perfected
Limits unreviewed for years on major accounts
evidence: Limit master data and change log

risk: Orders are accepted that the organisation cannot fulfil, should not accept, or that carry terms never approved.
audit_objective: Confirm orders are accepted within approved commercial and credit parameters.
what_to_review: Order entry authorisation and completeness of order data
Blocked-order release and who performs it
Non-standard terms — payment terms, delivery, penalties, retention
Availability and fulfilment feasibility checks
Order acknowledgement and contract formation
procedures: Test blocked orders released in the period and inspect the approval for each.
Sample orders with non-standard terms and trace the approval against delegated authority.
Reconcile orders entered to orders acknowledged and fulfilled; investigate orders cancelled after entry.
Test whether penalty and service-credit clauses accepted at order stage are tracked operationally.
red_flags: Blocks released by sales staff
Non-standard terms agreed by email without approval
Orders entered then cancelled repeatedly at period end
Penalty clauses accepted with no one monitoring performance

risk: Prices, discounts and rebates are applied outside approved authority, eroding margin invisibly one transaction at a time.
audit_objective: Confirm invoiced prices reflect approved price lists and that discounts and rebates are authorised and earned.
what_to_review: Price list maintenance and approval
Discount authority by role and value
Manual price overrides at invoicing
Rebate and volume incentive agreements and their accrual
Margin analysis by customer, product and salesperson
procedures: Re-price a sample of invoices from the approved price list and quantify the variance.
Analyse manual price overrides by user and customer; test the largest against approval authority.
Recompute rebates earned against agreements and test the accrual.
Analyse margin by customer and salesperson and investigate the loss-making tail.
Test whether price list changes were approved before activation.
red_flags: Discounts clustered just under an approval threshold
Overrides concentrated with one user
Rebates accrued on volumes never achieved
Customers persistently below cost to serve

risk: Goods or services are recorded as delivered when they are not, or delivery is recorded in the wrong period, misstating revenue.
audit_objective: Confirm delivery is evidenced and recorded in the correct period.
what_to_review: Proof of delivery capture and retention
Cut-off procedures at period end
Goods despatched but not invoiced, and invoiced but not despatched
Consignment, bill-and-hold and agency arrangements
Delivery to third-party warehouses or agents
procedures: Test cut-off either side of period end by tracing despatch documents to invoices and to the revenue period recorded.
Reconcile despatches to invoices for the period and age the unbilled and un-despatched populations.
Test the existence of proof of delivery for a sample of the largest period-end sales.
Review bill-and-hold and consignment arrangements against the criteria for recognising revenue.
red_flags: A concentration of large despatches on the final days of the period
Proof of delivery missing for the largest transactions
Consignment stock treated as sold
Delivery dates amended after invoicing
evidence: Despatch records and proof of delivery

risk: Deliveries are never invoiced, or invoices are issued with errors that delay payment and trigger disputes.
audit_objective: Confirm every delivery is invoiced once, accurately, and on time.
what_to_review: Completeness of invoicing against delivery
Invoice accuracy — quantity, price, tax, currency, customer details
Timeliness of invoicing after delivery
Sequence control over invoice numbering
Manual and pro-forma invoices outside the main system
procedures: Reconcile delivered volumes to invoiced volumes and quantify the unbilled population and its ageing.
Test invoice numerical sequence for gaps and duplicates.
Sample invoices and re-perform the calculation including tax treatment and currency.
Identify invoices raised outside the main system and test their control and recording.
Measure days from delivery to invoice by business unit.
red_flags: Unbilled deliveries ageing beyond the billing cycle
Gaps in invoice sequence with no explanation
Manual invoices used routinely for particular customers
Recurring disputes traced to invoice errors

risk: Credit notes are issued to conceal uncollectable debt, to reverse fictitious sales, or without any authorisation.
audit_objective: Confirm credit notes and adjustments are justified, supported and authorised independently.
what_to_review: Credit note authorisation limits and independence from sales and collections
Reason codes and their integrity
Credit notes issued after period end against prior-period sales
Returns received and their restocking or scrapping
Write-offs disguised as credit notes
procedures: Analyse credit notes by issuer, customer, value and reason code; test the largest and the most frequent.
Test credit notes raised after period end against sales recorded in the prior period.
Match credit notes for returns to physical evidence that goods came back.
Test whether credit notes are being used in place of a bad debt write-off, which would bypass the write-off authority.
red_flags: Credit notes concentrated shortly after period end
Reason code "other" dominating
Credits issued by the collector chasing the debt
No goods returned against return-reason credits
evidence: Credit note register with user and reason

risk: Receipts are misapplied or left unapplied, concealing lapping, misappropriation or genuinely overdue balances.
audit_objective: Confirm receipts are applied promptly and accurately to the correct customer and invoice.
what_to_review: Timeliness of cash application and the size of unapplied cash
Segregation between cash application, credit control and bank reconciliation
Write-off of small differences and unallocated amounts
Bank reconciliation quality and reconciling item ageing
Lapping indicators across customer accounts
procedures: Age the unapplied and on-account cash and test the reason for the oldest items.
Test that the person applying cash cannot raise credit notes or write off balances.
Analyse receipt application timing for patterns consistent with lapping — receipts applied to progressively older invoices.
Test bank reconciliations for aged reconciling items and unexplained adjustments.
Recompute small-difference write-offs against the tolerance policy.
red_flags: Unapplied cash growing period on period
Receipts routinely applied several days late
One person handling receipts, application and write-offs
Reconciling items carried forward for months
evidence: Cash application records and unapplied cash ageing

risk: Overdue balances are not pursued on schedule and disputes are left unresolved, so recoverable amounts become bad debts.
audit_objective: Assess whether collection activity and dispute resolution are timely, escalated and effective.
what_to_review: Dunning and escalation timetable and adherence to it
Collector workload, targets and performance
Dispute logging, ownership and resolution time
Stop-supply and legal escalation decisions
Use of external collection agencies and their recovery rates
procedures: Test whether escalation steps actually occurred at the policy trigger points for a sample of overdue accounts.
Analyse ageing and recovery performance by collector and by business unit.
Age disputed balances and test the resolution of the oldest; disputes often mask a delivery or invoicing failure.
Test whether stop-supply rules were applied or overridden, and by whom.
Compare recovery rates before and after referral to external agencies.
red_flags: Promises to pay recorded repeatedly with no follow-through
Disputes open beyond ninety days with no owner
Stop-supply overridden for the largest debtors
Accounts referred to agencies only once they are uncollectable
evidence: Aged receivables and collector activity notes

risk: The provision for doubtful debts is understated and write-offs are approved without authority, delaying recognition of losses.
audit_objective: Confirm the provision reflects genuine recoverability and that write-offs are properly authorised.
what_to_review: Provision methodology — ageing based, specific, or expected credit loss
Consistency of application and any management overlay
Write-off authority and evidence of recovery effort before write-off
Recovery of amounts previously written off
Balances with no movement or activity
procedures: Recompute the provision using the stated methodology and test the basis of any management override.
Sample write-offs and test the authority level and the recovery steps taken beforehand.
Identify aged balances not provided for and test the justification, including reliance on informal assurances.
Test subsequent receipts against previously written-off accounts, which can indicate premature write-off or misappropriated recoveries.
red_flags: Aged balances excluded from provision on the basis of a verbal assurance
Write-offs approved by the credit manager alone
Recoveries after write-off retained outside the ledger
Provision percentage unchanged despite a deteriorating book

risk: Revenue is recognised on terms that do not reflect the contract — before obligations are met, gross where the organisation acts as agent, or without allocating to separate obligations.
audit_objective: Confirm revenue recognition reflects the substance of customer contracts.
what_to_review: Identification of performance obligations in customer contracts
Timing — point in time versus over time
Gross versus net presentation where a third party is involved
Variable consideration, rebates, penalties and refund rights
Side agreements and non-standard terms outside the contract file
procedures: Read a sample of significant contracts and test whether recognition follows the obligations and terms actually written.
Test arrangements involving a third party for principal versus agent indicators and the resulting presentation.
Test the estimation of variable consideration and whether constraints were applied.
Enquire of sales staff about side letters and verbal commitments, and search correspondence for terms absent from the contract file.
Test contracts modified near period end for their effect on recognition.
red_flags: Side letters granting return rights not in the master contract
Gross presentation where the organisation carries no inventory risk
Long-term contracts recognised on invoicing rather than progress
Contract modifications concentrated at period end
